indication.label: Indication (FDA-labeled diagnosis)
indication.hint: Closed list from Alaska Medicaid Adbry criteria, effective 2024-06-01; topical prescription therapies inadequately control disease or are not advisable.

prescriber_specialty.label: Prescriber or consulting specialist
prescriber_specialty.hint: Must be prescribed by or in consultation with an allergist, immunologist, or dermatologist.

ad_bsa_severity_documented.label: AD: baseline BSA affected and symptom severity documented

ad_topical_failures.label: AD: tried/failed or contraindication (≥2 for 30 days)
ad_topical_failures.hint: Select therapies tried and failed for at least 30 days or contraindicated. At least two of TCS / TCI / PDE4 are required. The remaining-agents contraindication option attests to a distinct remaining class; do not double-count a selected class. The PDF does not specify TCS potency at exactly age 18.

not_used_with_another_biologic.label: Not used with another biologic (e.g. Enbrel, Dupixent, Xolair)

criteria.text: Diagnosis is moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, inadequately controlled with topical prescription therapies or when those therapies are not advisable.
Patient meets FDA-labeled age for Adbry: at least 12 years.
Prescribed by or in consultation with an allergist, immunologist, or dermatologist.

Baseline affected BSA AND symptom severity documented; tried and failed for 30 days or contraindication to at least two of: TCS (medium–high potency if >18 years / low potency if <18 years), topical calcineurin inhibitor, PDE4 inhibitor.
Denial if used in conjunction with another biologic medication (e.g. Enbrel, Dupixent, Xolair).

max_units.notes: First month: up to 1200 mg (eight 150 mg injections); thereafter up to 600 mg (four 150 mg injections) monthly. Initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 12 months. Quantity limits are not numeric predicates.

notes: Partial encoding from AK Adbry (tralokinumab-ldrm), an IL-13 antagonist, Criteria Version 1 (Original 02/27/2024, Accepted 04/19/2024, Effective 06/1/2024).

Encoded: closed moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis indication; FDA age ≥12 years; specialty or consultation; baseline affected BSA and symptom severity documentation; at least two topical classes tried/failed for 30 days or contraindicated; no concomitant biologic. Failure to meet approval criteria results in denial.

Attestation only, not numeric predicates: BSA percentage, symptom severity, topical potency and 30-day trial duration, contraindications, and monthly quantity math. TCS wording follows the PDF (>18 years medium–high potency; <18 years low potency); exactly age 18 is unspecified. Shared Dupixent AD option values are retained.

Duration notes only: initial approval up to 3 months; reauthorization up to 12 months. The PDF specifies no additional reauthorization response predicate. Cautions (hypersensitivity, eye symptoms, live vaccines, helminth infection) are not encoded as approval gates.
Alternatives: Dupixent is evaluate()-linked for overlapping atopic dermatitis. Adbry is PDL preferred in IMMUNOMODULATORS, ATOPIC DERMATITIS.
